title: Detection Tuning Trade-Off Explorer
description: Interactive p5.js simulation showing how moving a detection threshold across overlapping benign and malicious anomaly-score distributions trades true positives against false positives, false negatives, and daily alert volume, with a live ROC operating point.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity
chapter_title: "Network Security Foundations: Protocols, Firewalls, and Detection"

educational.topic: Intrusion detection tuning, false positives, false negatives, and alert fatigue
learningObjectives: Analyze how moving a detection threshold trades true-positive rate against false-positive rate.
Relate false-positive rate and traffic volume to the daily alert workload of an operations team.
Explain why a low base rate of attacks makes most alerts false even for a good detector.
Distinguish tuning a threshold from improving the detector's ability to separate benign and malicious activity.
educational.prerequisites: The difference between an IDS and an IPS; the definitions of true positive, false positive, and false negative.

pedagogical.assessment: Discussion questions in the lesson plan ask students to find the threshold a three-analyst team can sustain and to explain the base-rate effect in the alert-volume readout.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing a detector can be tuned to catch every attack with no false alarms.
Assuming a low false-positive rate means few false alerts, ignoring traffic volume and the base rate of attacks.
Treating threshold tuning and detector quality as the same lever.

controls.label: Threshold
controls.range: 0.00 to 1.00, step 0.01, default 0.50; also draggable on the plot

model.assumptions: Benign and malicious anomaly scores follow normal distributions with means 0.3 and 0.7 and a shared standard deviation, truncated to the 0-1 score axis; 1% of events are malicious.
model.limitations: A two-Gaussian teaching model, not a measured detector. Real score distributions are rarely normal, attack base rates are usually far below 1%, and alerts are deduplicated and correlated before an analyst sees them.
